root_cause.text: The driver fails to validate hardware-provided queue reader/writer indices against REMOTE_QUEUE_SIZE before using them to compute an MMIO address, allowing an out-of-bounds MMIO read when a compromised service processor supplies an out-of-range index.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (reader >= REMOTE_QUEUE_SIZE || writer >= REMOTE_QUEUE_SIZE)` at the top of the loop in `ibmasm_handle_mouse_interrupt()`, before calling `get_queue_entry()` which performs `queue_begin + reader * sizeof(struct remote_input)` without any prior validation. The commit message explicitly states this as the root cause.

candidates.rationale: Reads the writer index from hardware without validation, allowing an out-of-range value that bypasses the loop guard and leads to out-of-bounds access.

Uses the unchecked reader and writer indices in the loop condition; if writer is out of range, the loop may run erroneously or not at all, but the core issue is the lack of bounds checking before use in the next line.
Directly passes the unchecked reader index to get_queue_entry, which computes an MMIO address; an out-of-range index leads to out-of-bounds MMIO read.
Completes the memcpy call that uses the unchecked address; while the size constant is safe, the entire read operation is tainted by the invalid address from the previous line.

vuln_statements.explanation: The writer index is read from hardware without validation against REMOTE_QUEUE_SIZE, allowing an out-of-range value that leads to out-of-bounds MMIO access.

The loop condition uses the unchecked reader and writer indices. If writer is out of range, the loop may not behave as intended, but more critically the unchecked indices are used in the loop body's memory access.

The unchecked reader index is passed directly to get_queue_entry, which computes an MMIO address based on that index and REMOTE_QUEUE_SIZE. Without validation, an out-of-range index results in an out-of-bounds MMIO read.

This completes the memcpy call that uses the potentially invalid address from the previous line. The size constant is safe, but the overall read operation becomes an out-of-bounds access due to the unchecked index.

Author: Max Asbock <masbock@us.ibm.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 21 17:16:34 2005 -0700

    [PATCH] ibmasm driver: redesign handling of remote control events
    
    This patch rewrites the handling of remote control events.  Rather than making
    them available from a special file in the ibmasmfs, now the events from the
    RSA card get translated into kernel input events and injected into the input
    subsystem.  The driver now will generate two /dev
bic_trace_step.reason: The new `ibmasm_handle_mouse_interrupt` function (lines after diff) still calls `get_queue_reader(sp)` and `get_queue_writer(sp)` to obtain hardware-provided indices and uses them in `get_queue_entry(sp, reader)` to calculate an MMIO address (via `memcpy_fromio`). There is no bounds check against `REMOTE_QUEUE_SIZE` before accessing the entry, so an out-of-range index from a compromised service processor can cause an out-of-bounds MMIO read. The vulnerable construct remains and no fix has been applied.
